problem: Given that $u=x-1$, which integral is equivalent to $\int x\sqrt[5]{x-1}\,\text{d}x?$
worked_solution:
Since $u=x-1,$ then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=u+1.$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt[5]{x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (u+1)(\sqrt[5]{u})(\text{d}u) \\  & =\int (u+1)({u}^{1/5})(\text{d}u) \\  & =\int ({u}^{6/5}+{u}^{1/5})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$
